properties.details_shown: Fog, tar, and gulls; the far piers are rotting. In the morning fog still sits on the docks, with gulls everywhere; the party seeks a boat at the end of pier four.

sources.quote: Morning in Gullwick. The fog is still sitting on the docks, gulls everywhere, and you're standing at the end of pier four looking for a boat.

changes.why: Adds the morning view and pier four to the established docks.

properties.role: Tide-reader who offers to row the party to the old chapel
properties.played_as: Whispers as if the water might hear her, avoids eye contact, keeps her gaze on the tide line; grey braid and salt-stained coat, mending a net.
properties.wants: Will row the party by day, never at night; offers to meet at pier four tomorrow at first light.
properties.knows: Says her boat is the only one that goes near the bell water because the others are scared; says Saltmere flooded the night the bell first rang forty years ago, and recalls her grandmother saying the water came up warm.

sources.quote: There's a woman sitting on an upturned skiff, mending a net. Grey braid, salt-stained coat. She doesn't look up.
Sela Thorn. I read the tides. I'll row you, but not at night. Never at night.
She talks in a whisper, like the water might hear her, and she never once looks you in the eye. She keeps her gaze on the tide line.
Sella's boat is the only one that goes near the bell water. The others are scared.
Sela, Sella, the dockhands say it both ways.
Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.
She shrugs and goes back to her net. She says she'll be at pier four tomorrow at first light if you want the ride.

changes.why: Records the new voiced NPC, her manner, alternate spelling, claims, and offered passage.

properties.details_shown: Previously described as having sunk into the bay with its bell. At low water the roof sticks out of the bay, with the bell tower and two broken arches; seaweed hangs from the stones. At midnight the underwater bell rings twelve times and the humming is much louder than two nights before, felt in the teeth. Pale shapes stand in rows on the submerged chapel floor like a congregation, then vanish when the bell stops.

sources.quote: The drowned chapel's roof sticks out of the bay at low water, just the bell tower and two broken arches. Seaweed hangs from the stones.
And then, right at midnight, the bell rings again under the water. Twelve times. And the humming is back, but louder. Much louder than two nights ago. You can feel it in your teeth.
Shapes. Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation. Then the bell stops and they're gone.

changes.why: Adds the GM's visible chapel details and the witnessed midnight event.
